long_biography.plain_text:
Reading philosophy during Army service became a practical investment tool for American investor William H. “Bill” Miller III. He later studied it at Johns Hopkins and credits that training with strengthening his analytical habits. At the Santa Fe Institute, research into adaptive systems guided his early interest in technology companies and shaped a broader interpretation of value investing.

Miller turned those intellectual interests into durable institutions. His endowments expanded Johns Hopkins programmes in philosophy and physics, while support for the Santa Fe Institute funded complexity-science research and a dedicated campus. He now serves as a Johns Hopkins trustee and as life trustee and chairman emeritus of the Santa Fe Institute.
